title: Sarde a beccafico
subtitle: Sicilian stuffed sardines
excerpt: Fresh sardines opened flat, stuffed with a sweet-savoury Sicilian filling of pine nuts, raisins, capers, and breadcrumbs, then rolled and baked. A dish of startling elegance from humble ingredients.
sourceNotes: Sarde a beccafico is a classic Palermitan dish; the name refers to the fig-pecker bird (beccafico), which was said to eat figs all day and had a plump, fat belly. The stuffed sardines resemble the bird. Cross-referenced with Anna Del Conte, Gastronomy of Italy (1987) and Mary Taylor Simeti, Pomp and Sustenance: Twenty-Five Centuries of Sicilian Food (1989).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sardines can be stuffed and rolled up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerated unbaked.

content.text: Sarde a beccafico is one of the signature dishes of Palermo. Fresh sardines are butterflied open, filled with a mixture of toasted breadcrumbs, pine nuts, raisins, capers, and anchovies, then rolled up and packed tightly in a baking dish with bay leaves between them and baked quickly. Ask the fishmonger to clean and butterfly the sardines if you don't want to do this yourself.

items.prepNote: about 12 to 16 sardines, cleaned and butterflied open, heads and backbones removed
divided: 30 ml for the filling, 30 ml to dress the dish
fresh or dried, one per sardine roll
juice of 1 for the dish, 1 cut into wedges to serve

content.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (180°C conventional, gas 6). Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until golden. Remove to a bowl.

Combine the toasted breadcrumbs with the pine nuts, raisins, capers, anchovies, parsley, orange zest, 30 ml olive oil, and a little salt and pepper. Stir well. The filling should be moist and hold together.

Lay the butterflied sardines skin side down. Place a heaped teaspoon of filling at the wider end of each sardine. Roll from the head end towards the tail, so the tail sticks up. Secure with a cocktail stick if needed.
Pack the rolls tightly in a baking dish with a bay leaf between each one, all upright so the tails point up. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and the juice of 1 lemon. Season.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the tops are golden and the fish is just cooked through. Serve hot or warm, with lemon wedges.

items.symptom: The sardines fall apart when rolling
items.fix: Use a cocktail stick to secure each roll. Or use large sardines which are easier to work with.
Add a tablespoon more olive oil and stir. The filling should hold together when pressed.
Reduce the raisins to 30 g. The sweet-sour balance should lean slightly toward savour.
15 minutes is often enough for medium sardines. Check at 12 minutes; the flesh should flake easily.

content.text: Sarde a beccafico is one of the emblematic dishes of Sicilian cooking, particularly associated with Palermo. The combination of sweet (raisins, orange zest) and salty-savoury (anchovies, capers) in a breadcrumb filling is a hallmark of the agrodolce (sweet-sour) tradition that runs through all Sicilian cookery and derives from Arab influence on the island's medieval cuisine. The dish is economical: sardines are cheap, the filling extends them, and the result is something far greater than its ingredients suggest.
